Willd. |synonyms_ref = {{GRIN | accessdate=2010-08-03}} }} '''''Talinum fruticosum''''' is a [[Herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant]] that is native to [[Mexico]], the [[Caribbean]], [[West Africa]], [[Central America]], and much of [[South America]]. Common names include '''Ceylon spinach''',{{PLANTS|id=TATR2|taxon=Talinum triangulare|accessdate=7 December 2015}} '''waterleaf''', '''cariru''', '''Gbure''', '''Surinam purslane''', '''Philippine spinach''', '''Florida spinach''', '''potherb fameflower''', '''sweetheart, and Kutu bataw''' in [[Ghana]] from the [[Akan language]] . In Nigeria it is known as Mgbolodi in Igbo, Efo Gbure in Yoruba, Alenyruwa in Hausa,[https://infonet-biovision.org/indigenous-plants/waterleaf-new] and Moin-moin Ikong in Efik It is widely grown in tropical regions as a [[leaf vegetable]]. In the Mithila region of the Indian subcontinent, it is locally known as ''Raja Rani Saag''.{{Cite news |title=औषधीय गुणों से युक्त यह सब्जी बिलुप्त होने की कगार पर, अब कुत्ते कर रहे हैं इसकी रखवाली |url=https://hindi.news18.com/news/bihar/darbhanga-rani-vegetable-with-medicinal-properties-reaches-the-brink-of-extinction-7553745.html |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20230916233423/https://hindi.news18.com/news/bihar/darbhanga-rani-vegetable-with-medicinal-properties-reaches-the-brink-of-extinction-7553745.html |archive-date=2023-09-16 |access-date=2026-08-06 |work=News18 हिंदी |language=hi-IN}} [[File:Raja-Rani Saag.jpg|thumb|Raja Rani Saag kept for making [[Tarua]].]] == Description == The plant grows erect, reaching a height of {{convert|30|to|100|cm|in|abbr=on}}. It bears small, pink [[flower]]s and broad, fleshy [[leaf|leaves]]. == Uses == As a [[leaf vegetable]], ''T. fruticosum'' is rich in [[vitamin]]s, including [[vitamin A|vitamins A]] and [[vitamin C|C]], and [[dietary mineral|minerals]] such as [[iron]] and [[calcium]] {{Citation needed|date=March 2022}}. Because it is high in [[oxalic acid]], consumption should be avoided or limited by those suffering from [[kidney]] disorders, [[gout]], and [[rheumatoid arthritis]] {{Citation needed|date=March 2022}}. It is cultivated in [[West Africa]], [[South Asia]], [[Southeast Asia]], and the warmer parts of [[North America|North]] and [[South America]]. In [[Brazil]] it is grown along the banks of the [[Amazon River]], and is consumed mainly in the states of [[Pará]] and [[Amazonas State, Brazil|Amazonas]]. In the Mithila region of the Indian subcontinent, its leaves are used to make vegetables and fritters.
